title: Higher direct image bound from affine etale inverse images
statement: Let $g:X\to Y$ be any scheme morphism and $c\in\mathbf N$. Suppose that for every affine scheme $W$ and etale morphism $w:W\to Y$, the fibre product $W\times_YX$ has all-torsion etale cohomological dimension at most $c$ [def-sc-etale-torsion-cd, def-pc-fibre-product]. Then for every locally torsion abelian sheaf $F$ on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ and every integer $q>c$, the higher direct image $R^qg_*F$ is zero [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. No quasi-compactness or finite-type condition on $g$ is imposed.

proof.text: Use the exact equivalence between abelian sheaves and sheaves of ULift Z-modules. The source isZero_higherDirectImage_of_forall_isAffine criterion reduces vanishing to cohomology over each affine etale target object. For the base-changed etale source object V, transfer the assumed derived-section bound to Sheaf.H using nonempty_sheafH_extDerivedIso. The underlying abelian inverse image is torsion by upperStarForget2 and preservation of torsion. The source subsingleton_ext_freeSheaf_of_subsingleton_H_of_acyclic applies because injective integer-module sheaves have acyclic underlying abelian sheaves. The Ext/free-sheaf and shifted single-functor equivalences give the required presheaf vanishing. Finally transport through the exact equivalence and its compatibility with derived direct image, single-degree embeddings and homology. The source affine-object criterion is the sheafification/local-generation argument of the original step 10.

theorem isZero_higherDirectImage_of_affineEtale_cd {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (g : X ⟶ Y)
    (c : ℕ)
    (hc : ∀ {W : Scheme.{u}} (w : W ⟶ Y) [Etale w] [IsAffine W],
      Scheme.HasTorsionEtaleCohomologicalDimensionLE (pullback w g) c)
    (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) (hF : F.IsTorsion)
    (q : ℤ) (hq : (c : ℤ) < q) :
    IsZero ((DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor
        (Sheaf Y.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) q).obj
      ((Etale.lowerStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} g).rightDerivedFunctorPlus.obj
        ((DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctor _ 0).obj F)))
